source_title: MLC Election Results: BJP Faces Opposition Offensive as SP Claims Momentum Ahead of 2027 UP Polls
source_excerpt:
The results of the 28 Legislative Council seats across four states have triggered a fresh political battle, with opposition parties targeting the BJP over its defeats in several high-profile constituencies. In Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party has improved its performance, winning five of the 11 MLC seats, while the BJP has retained six. The final Varanasi Graduate result was still awaiting formal announcement in the update, although the BJP candidate had reportedly conceded defeat. SP spokesperson Anurag Bhadauria linked the party's victories in Kashi, Mathura and Prayagraj to divine blessings, arguing that the Samajwadi Party follows the ideals associated with Lord Ram, while accusing the BJP of using religion for political gains. Congress spokesperson Surendra Rajput also attacked the BJP, referring to the party's earlier political slogan about Ayodhya, Mathura and Kashi and claiming that recent results had delivered a message to the ruling party. The BJP responded through Union Minister BL Verma, who questioned Akhilesh Yadav's political position on Sanatan traditions and Muslim appeasement. The results have also drawn attention to defeats in other major constituencies. In Maharashtra, the Maha Vikas Aghadi won three of the five MLC seats, while the ruling Mahayuti secured two. Congress won the high-profile Nagpur Teacher seat, while the RJD registered a victory in the Patna Graduate constituency in Bihar. Opposition leaders have used these outcomes to question the BJP's political strength, particularly in constituencies associated with prominent leaders and religious centres. In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP won the Lucknow Teacher, Bareilly-Moradabad Teacher, Meerut Graduate, Agra Graduate, Gorakhpur Teacher and Meerut Teacher seats. The SP won the Varanasi Teacher, Varanasi Graduate, Allahabad-Jhansi Graduate, Lucknow Graduate and Agra Teacher seats, according to the reported final tally. The caste composition of the winning candidates has also become part of the political debate. The BJP's six winners reportedly include three Brahmins, one Rajput, one Vaishya and one Sikh, while the SP's five include two Yadavs, one Kayastha, one Vaishya and one Kurmi. The SP is presenting the results as a boost to its PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) strategy.
